claims.text: The starting material is an as-cast refractory high-entropy alloy.
The intervention is the addition of 2 at.% boron.
Adding 2 at.% boron to the refractory high-entropy alloy will form boride precipitates.
Dislocation pinning will reduce dislocation mobility and thereby increase strength.
Relative to the as-cast alloy without boron, 2 at.% boron will increase high-temperature yield strength by 15%.
The predicted strength improvement will hold from 800 to 1000°C under loads of 100 to 500 MPa.
Adding 2 at.% boron will increase density by less than 1%.
Adding 2 at.% boron will cause no significant change in room-temperature mechanical performance.
The relevant baseline is the same as-cast refractory high-entropy alloy without boron.
A tensile comparison at 900°C and 200 MPa can test the boron-added alloy against the as-cast baseline.
The hypothesis is falsified if the boron-added alloy has less than a 10% yield-strength improvement or more than a 2% density increase.

contradictions.description: The prediction specifies a 15% strength improvement, but the experiment falsifies only improvements below 10%. Results from 10% to below 15% would violate the stated prediction without falsifying it.
The prediction limits density increase to less than 1%, whereas falsification requires an increase above 2%. A 1–2% increase would violate the hypothesis but not meet its falsification rule.
